title: Grade 4 Science — Fri, Jun 27
description: Food and Digestion — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review
subject: science

questions.question: Digestion begins in which organ?
questions.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth — both mechanical (chewing) and chemical (salivary amylase breaks down starch).

questions.question: Which enzyme in saliva begins starch digestion?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase begins breaking down starch (carbohydrate) into simpler sugars in the mouth.

questions.question: The food pipe connecting mouth to stomach is called:
questions.explanation: The oesophagus (food pipe) transports the bolus from the mouth to the stomach using peristalsis.

questions.question: Which nutrient does protein-rich food provide? Give an Indian food example.
questions.explanation: Proteins provide growth and repair. Dal (lentils) is an excellent plant-based protein source commonly eaten in Indian meals.

questions.question: The main job of the small intestine is:
options: To absorb digested nutrients into the blood
questions.explanation: The small intestine is the primary absorption site — nutrients pass through its villi-lined wall into the bloodstream.

questions.question: Teeth: which type GRINDS food?
questions.explanation: Molars (and premolars) are large, flat teeth designed for grinding and crushing food. Incisors cut; canines tear.

questions.question: Bile is produced by the ___ and stored in the ___.
questions.explanation: Bile is made by the liver, stored in the gallbladder, and released into the small intestine to emulsify (break up) fats.

questions.question: A balanced diet must include all of these EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre. Pesticides are chemical contaminants — NOT a nutrient.

questions.question: Sequence: What is the correct order of the digestive path?
options: Mouth → Stomach → Oesophagus → Small intestine → Large intestine
Mouth → Oesophagus → Stomach → Small intestine → Large intestine
Stomach → Mouth → Oesophagus → Large intestine → Small intestine
Oesophagus → Mouth → Stomach → Small intestine → Large intestine
questions.explanation: Correct path: Mouth → Oesophagus → Stomach → Small intestine (absorption) → Large intestine (water) → Anus. This is the standard digestive route.

questions.question: What is the semi-liquid formed in the stomach called? And what is the ball of food formed in the mouth called?
questions.explanation: Mouth: chewed food + saliva = BOLUS. Stomach: bolus + gastric juice (churned) = CHYME. Two different terms for two different stages.

questions.question: Why is Vitamin D important and how is it made?
options: Helps absorb calcium for strong bones; made by skin in sunlight
Digests fat; made in the liver
questions.explanation: Vitamin D helps absorb calcium → strong bones and teeth. Uniquely, it is synthesised in skin exposed to sunlight. Deficiency causes rickets in children.

questions.question: Why does the small intestine have villi?
options: To greatly increase surface area for faster absorption of nutrients
questions.explanation: Villi = tiny finger-like projections that multiply the surface area of the small intestine enormously. More surface area = faster, more complete absorption of digested nutrients.

questions.question: A child eats a mango, some roti and a glass of milk. Which part of the meal gives PROTEIN?
questions.explanation: Milk = rich in protein (casein and whey) + calcium. Roti = carbohydrate. Mango = vitamins (A, C), carbohydrate, fibre. For protein, milk is the correct answer.

questions.question: Iron deficiency causes anaemia. Which food should an anaemic child eat more of?
questions.explanation: Iron-rich foods: spinach (palak), pomegranate, dates (khajoor), lentils (dal), jaggery (gur). These are common Indian iron sources — important for anaemia prevention.

questions.question: Complete the nutrient match: Carbohydrates=___ · Proteins=___ · Calcium=___ · Vitamin C=___ · Iron=___
options: Energy · Growth · Strong bones · Immunity · Oxygen transport
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates = energy. Proteins = growth/repair. Calcium = strong bones/teeth. Vitamin C = immunity/prevents scurvy. Iron = haemoglobin in red blood cells (oxygen transport).
